The macOS count above rests on a name heuristic, so it is not the
primary evidence. The primary evidence is the per-release listing
earlier in this file: every one of these asset names can be read by
eye. They comprise Windows binary/symbol archives, Linux archives
(including preview and clang-cl variants), and dxil.zip on the 2017
alpha. None has a macOS-shaped name.

========================================================================
POSITIVE CONTROL for the macOS classifier
========================================================================
'0 macOS assets' is an ABSENCE result, and an absence result from a
classifier that cannot recognise the thing it is looking for is
worthless. So: names macOS assets would plausibly carry, run through
the same classify() used above. Every line must say macos.
    OK               macos  macos_dxc_2026_07_29.arm64.tar.gz
    OK       macos+windows  dxc_2026_07_29_macOS.zip
    OK       macos+windows  dxc-universal-apple-darwin.tar.gz
    OK       macos+windows  dxc_aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
    OK       macos+windows  dxc-osx-x86_64.tar.gz
    OK               macos  DirectXShaderCompiler.dmg
    OK       macos+windows  dxc-1.9.2607.pkg

    control result: PASS - the zero above is a real zero

Negative half of the control: no name actually present on a release
classifies as macOS, which is the finding. The two halves together
say the classifier discriminates rather than always answering no.
